purpose: Section 18: certify that the Phase 3F.1.5.R persisted safe-failure models (ClaimReviewItem/ClaimReviewObservation/ClaimReviewDecision) actually work as designed against real Postgres. This artifact does NOT merely re-trust the prior phase's own claims - it re-runs the prior phase's own adversarial test file, then independently constructs and executes a SEPARATE verification script written fresh by this auditor.

environment.database: real Postgres, localhost:5432, database 'headroom', migration 20260829232147_phase_3f1_5_r_claim_review_safe_failure applied and verified via `npx prisma migrate status` (schema up to date)
environment.note: This auditor's worktree was initially checked out on a stale, divergent branch (worktree-agent-a792d754f1cba6b0b @ 81fd6c4) that never received the Phase 3F.1.5.R commits at all (schema.prisma had zero ClaimReviewItem references). Corrected by creating a fresh local branch 'cert-3f1-6-audit-a792d754' from the assigned starting commit ea82ee80f4528117e7dc6669be8e1ebf28b24108 before any audit work began. Disclosed here because it is directly relevant to trusting the rest of this artifact's findings.

independentVerificationScript.description: Auditor-authored, not derived from or reusing the prior phase's own test assertions. 26 independent checks (labeled A-G) covering: raw-SQL persistence bypassing the Prisma client entirely; tenant scope in BOTH directions (two companies CAN each hold a row for the identical claimKey as two separate rows; the DB's own @@unique constraint, not just application logic, rejects a duplicate (companyId, claimKey) row); source provenance non-emptiness on a freshly created item; dedup with a genuinely different reason (OBSERVATION_APPENDED, exactly 2 observation rows); a TWO-cycle resolve/reopen lifecycle (ACCEPT -> REOPEN -> REJECT -> REOPEN) confirming every original observation/decision row survives verbatim and the item fails open (OPEN_REVIEW) after the second reopen, not just the first; and no-sibling-substitution across two distinct claims where only one is resolved.
independentVerificationScript.cleanup: Verified via a direct psql COUNT query after the run: 0 rows remained under the scratch company ids.

findings.evidence: recordClaimReview() creates a row confirmed present via a raw prisma.$queryRaw SQL SELECT against claim_review_items, bypassing the ORM's own return value entirely.
Same claimKey + same company recorded twice -> ALREADY_RECORDED, one row, one observation. Confirmed both via the prior phase's own test and this auditor's independent script.

Two different companyIds sharing the identical claimKey produce TWO separate rows (findMany on claimKey alone returns 2 rows, with 2 distinct ids) - not merged, not silently collapsed. A raw duplicate-row INSERT attempt for the SAME company + claimKey pair that already has a row is rejected by the database's own @@unique([companyId, claimKey]) constraint (Prisma error code P2002), not merely prevented by service.ts's own application-level check - i.e. this is a constraint-level guarantee, not just a convention.

findings.result: PASS, with one disclosed schema-vs-practice nuance
findings.evidence: sourceEvidence, sourceCitation, rationale, and algorithmVersion are all non-empty on every created item in both test suites. sourceEvidence, rationale, and algorithmVersion are NOT NULL at the schema level (prisma/schema.prisma: String, not String?). sourceCitation is schema-nullable (String?) and service.ts/types.ts's own ClaimReviewItemInput type allows null - HOWEVER derive.ts's only real derivation path (deriveFromCoverageEntry) sources sourceCitation from SourceAnchor.sourceCitation, which is itself a REQUIRED (non-optional) string on SourceAnchor - so in practice, via the one wired derivation path, sourceCitation can never actually be null for a review item created from real coverage-audit output. The null-permitting type is defensive/future-proofing, not a currently reachable gap.

recordClaimReview called twice with the same claimKey but a genuinely different (reasonCode, rationale) pair -> OBSERVATION_APPENDED, one item, exactly two observation rows confirmed via a fresh findUniqueOrThrow read-back.

Static grep of lib/contract-model/compiler/safe-failure/service.ts and integrate.ts for `.delete`, `deleteMany`, `.update(`, `updateMany` finds exactly two `.update()` calls, BOTH against `claimReviewItem` only (never `claimReviewObservation` or `claimReviewDecision`), and zero delete calls of any kind anywhere in the module. Independently confirmed at runtime: after a 2-resolve/2-reopen cycle (3 observations, 4 decisions total), the FIRST observation's `detail` and the FIRST decision's `note` were read back byte-for-byte unchanged.

All three actions transition ClaimReviewItem.status correctly (RESOLVED_ACCEPTED/RESOLVED_REJECTED/SUPERSEDED) and each writes exactly one new ClaimReviewDecision row recording previousStatus/newStatus/note/decidedBy. Verified for all three actions across the two test suites.

findings.requirement: Supersession lifecycle interplay with P1-11 amendment supersession
findings.result: DISCLOSED GAP - manual-only, no automatic trigger
findings.evidence: Grepped the entire lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/** tree and every other reference to AmendmentEffect/amendment_effects in the repository for any call into recordClaimReview/resolveClaimReview/checkExplicitSafeFailure or any import of the safe-failure module: ZERO matches. resolveClaimReview(action='SUPERSEDE') exists and works correctly when called directly (tested), but nothing in the amendment pipeline (lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/pipeline.ts, chain.ts, deterministic-parser.ts, semantic-interpreter.ts, schedule-modification.ts, validation.ts) ever calls it. If a provision underlying an OPEN_REVIEW claim is later amended/superseded, the ClaimReviewItem row does NOT automatically transition to SUPERSEDED - it remains OPEN_REVIEW indefinitely unless a human (or some future, currently nonexistent, caller) explicitly calls resolveClaimReview with action=SUPERSEDE. This is an honest, disclosed limitation, not a hidden defect - the prior phase's own service.ts comments frame SUPERSEDE as a decision a caller invokes, not an automatic reaction to amendment events.
findings.recommendation: Not implemented by this auditor (production code frozen for this audit). A future phase wiring the amendment pipeline to call resolveClaimReview(SUPERSEDE) when a superseded provision's claimKey has an OPEN_REVIEW item would close this gap.

findings.evidence: Re-ran the prior phase's own reopen scenario (test 12/16) - passed. Additionally constructed a NEW, more demanding scenario in this auditor's own script: ACCEPT -> re-detect (REOPENED_FROM_RESOLVED) -> REJECT -> re-detect a SECOND time (REOPENED_FROM_RESOLVED again). Confirmed the item correctly reopens on BOTH cycles (not just once as a special case), ends at status OPEN_REVIEW, and accumulates 4 distinct decision rows (ACCEPT, REOPEN, REJECT, REOPEN) in the correct order, all preserved.

Constructed two fresh, independent claimKeys (not reused from the prior phase's own fixtures) under the same company/document/section-family. Resolved ONE via ACCEPT and left the other OPEN. checkExplicitSafeFailure() lookups for each returned their OWN row id and OWN (different) status - the resolved sibling's ACCEPT never leaked into or satisfied the other's lookup.

overallStatement: The persisted claim-level safe-failure model (ClaimReviewItem/ClaimReviewObservation/ClaimReviewDecision) functions correctly against real Postgres across every dimension in this section's charter: persistence, dedup, tenant isolation (including at the database constraint level, not merely application logic), source provenance, append-only history, full resolution lifecycle, and reopen-on-re-detection (including under repeated cycles). The one disclosed gap - amendment supersession does not automatically drive ClaimReviewItem.SUPERSEDED - is a manual-only capability today, not a defect in what exists; it is rated MINOR because resolveClaimReview(SUPERSEDE) itself works correctly when invoked, the gap is only in automatic triggering, which was never claimed to exist by the prior phase's own documentation.
